pll1d17c4-d1e3477.summary: Defines the mission: the Spirit is said to be sent or given when he is in us so as to make us love God and neighbor, by which we abide in God and God in us.
claims: The Spirit is given when he makes us love God and neighbor.
Through this love we abide in God and God in us.

pll1d17c4-d1e3480.summary: Cites De Trinitate XV: the Spirit who proceeds from God, when given to man, kindles him to love God and neighbor and is himself love, for man has no means to love God except from God. This is how the Spirit is given as gift.
claims: The Spirit given kindles love of God and neighbor.
The Spirit is himself that love.
Man can love God only from God.

pll1d17c4-d1e3503.summary: Further De Trinitate XV: charity poured into our hearts (Rom 5:5) is the most excellent gift, alone dividing children of the kingdom from children of perdition. Other gifts profit nothing without it (1 Cor 13). The Spirit is properly called gift only because of love, and through charity the whole Trinity dwells in us. Lombard concludes that the Spirit is given when he so exists in someone as to make him a lover of God and neighbor, and only then does one properly have the Spirit.
claims: Charity is the most excellent gift of God.
Charity alone separates the children of the kingdom from those of perdition.
Without charity other gifts do not lead to eternal life.
The Spirit is properly called gift because of charity.
The whole Trinity dwells in us through charity.
One properly has the Spirit when he makes one love God and neighbor.

pl-l1d17c4.summary: Defines the invisible mission: the Spirit is sent or given when he is in us so as to make us love God and neighbor, by which we abide in God and God in us. With Augustine, the Spirit given kindles love of God and neighbor and is that love, for man has nothing from which to love God except from God. Charity, poured into our hearts (Rom 5:5), is the most excellent gift, alone dividing the children of the kingdom from those of perdition; other gifts profit nothing without it (1 Cor 13). The Spirit is properly called gift because of charity, through which the whole Trinity dwells in us.
claims: The Spirit is sent or given when he is in us so as to make us love God and neighbor.
The Spirit given kindles love and is himself that love.
Man has nothing by which to love God except from God.
Charity is the most excellent gift and alone separates the saved from the lost.
Other gifts of the Spirit profit nothing without charity.
The Spirit is properly called gift because of charity.
Through charity the whole Trinity dwells in us.
